section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that for Rosh Hashanah, physical shofar blowing is required, encompassing both the straight ram's horn (representing self-nullification of all desires) and the bent ram's horn (representing the higher work of subjugation).
section.t: And behold, not only is physical action required
(and the spiritual aspect of teshuvah is not sufficient, nor even the recitation of verses),
but within this itself, it is not sufficient that it be the inner voice of man; rather, one must specifically blow with the sound of a ram's horn of an animal,
[either] a straight ram's horn or bent ram's horns,
according to the two opinions in this matter, for these and those are the words of the living G-d.
And also now,
when we blow
(on Rosh Hashanah)
with bent ram's horns,
there are these two aspects in the spiritual service.
[The aspect] of a straight ram's horn, because "the more a person straightens his mind, the better,"
and it is explained in Chassidus
that this is that a person must strip himself of all his desires.
And the intention is not [only] for undesirable desires,
for what would that teach us?
And this matter
(that he should have no undesirable desires)
is already accomplished through the service of the month of Elul before Rosh Hashanah.
And the matter of "a person straightens his mind" on Rosh Hashanah is that he should strip himself of every [mental] image, even an image of holiness.
For the drawing down of Rosh Hashanah is from that which is beyond the category of place and beyond the category of image,
therefore the service of "straightening" [stripping] is required,
and through the simplicity [self-nullification] within man, he draws down the simplicity above,
even reaching the aspect of the ultimate simplicity.
And we blow with bent ram's horns, because "the more a person bends his mind, the better,"
and it is explained in Chassidus
that this is the service of subjugation
(which has an advantage even over the service of stripping away desires),
that this service is through the aspect of "male"
(bent ram's horns),
"a man's way is to conquer."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the mitzvah of shofar on Rosh Hashanah draws down a new light that renews all of creation, accomplished specifically through the service of Israel, who are G-d's children.
section.t: And this is the mitzvah of the day with the shofar,
that through the service of the shofar in the two modes of "straightening" and "bending"
[each of which has a unique advantage]
they draw down a new light,
as explained in Iggeret HaKodesh
that on every Rosh Hashanah a new light is drawn down that never existed before,
and through this, renewal occurs in the entire order of the chain of descent,
even reaching renewal in the externality of the worlds.
And although the primary renewal on Rosh Hashanah is in the inwardness of the worlds,
nevertheless, through this, renewal occurs also in the externality of the worlds,
as explained in the Siddur
in the discourse "L’havin Inyan Teki’at Shofar al pi Kavvanat HaBaal Shem Tov z"l."
And all this is accomplished through Israel, "a people close to Him,"
"You are children to Hashem your G-d,"
as the Maggid explains in Likutei Amarim and Or HaTorah at their beginning, regarding the matter of "Whom He consulted? The souls of the righteous,"
that the delight He would take in the service of Israel arose before Him,
and this determined the [primordial] will,
and from the aspect of the absolute will it was drawn to the revealed will,
and afterwards it was drawn through the entire order of the chain of descent until this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower,
for specifically through this the intention of "a dwelling place for Him in the lower realms" is completed.
And this is the meaning of "Say before Me [verses of] Malchuyot so that you will coronate Me over you... and with what? With a shofar,"
which means the actual blowing of the shofar in deed,
for "the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,"
except that included in this
(in continuation of the beginning of the maamar, "Say before Me... and Shofarot")
is also the recitation of the verses of Shofarot,
[and particularly, according to this, one can reconcile our version in the Gemara with the version
"Say before Me [verses of] Malchuyot so that... Zichronot so that... Shofarot so that..." and the thirteen [shofar blasts] afterwards,
"and with what? With a shofar."]

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "And on your joyous days... you shall blow with trumpets" refers to the connection of the two halves of a form—G-d and Israel, and the higher and lower parts of each soul—uniting them before G-d.
section.t: And behold, this verse
("And on your joyous days... and you shall blow with trumpets...")
is the continuation and conclusion of the matter preceding it,
"Make for yourself two trumpets...,"
and the teaching of the Maggid is known,
"Two trumpets, two half-forms,"
meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel are,
[so to speak,
and perhaps even without "so to speak",]
two half-forms.
From this, the explanation of the verse is understood: "And you shall blow with trumpets... and they shall be for you as a remembrance before your G-d, I am Hashem your G-d,"
that the matter of Malchuyot
("I am Hashem your G-d")
and Zichronot
("and they shall be for you as a remembrance")
which is accomplished through "and you shall blow with trumpets,"
"With trumpets and the sound of the shofar, shout before the King, Hashem"
[for in the Temple
("before your G-d,"
"before the King, Hashem")
both were present
(except that the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,
as explained in the Mishnah),
and through the "latticed windows, unopenable" that were in the Temple,
this was drawn
(as all matters of the Temple)
also to the outlying areas, even to the entire world.
And even in the time of exile],
it is because the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel are two half-forms.
And the explanation is,
that the second soul in Israel is literally a part of G-d above,
and it is known
that there are two extremes in this.
For "literally" applies to "a part of G-d above,"
meaning that the second soul in Israel is a literal part of His very Essence [Atzmus],
and the Baal Shem Tov's statement is known,
"When you grasp a part of the essence, you grasp the whole of it,"
and the word "literally" also indicates the lowest extreme,
"literally" that which is grasped by the sense of touch.
And this is what it means that the second soul in Israel is literally a part of G-d above,
that even when it is clothed in a physical body, literally from the word "touch,"
even then it is a literal part of His Essence and Being, blessed be He,
one literal [unity] with His Essence [Atzmus],
and according to the teaching of the Maggid
(cited above)
that they are two half-forms.
And now, since "you are called 'man'"
on the name "similar to the One above,"
it is understood that the matter of two half-forms is also within the soul itself.
For it is known
that in every soul there are two general levels,
the part of the soul that is above
(the aspect of the mazal)
the "head" of the soul,
and the part of the soul that is in the body
(the revealed faculties)
the "foot" of the soul.
And these two aspects are the two half-forms within each particular soul.
And the meaning of "And you shall blow with trumpets... and they shall be for you as a remembrance before your G-d..." is that one must connect his two half-forms
and place them
(אַוועקשטעלן זיי)
before Hashem your G-d,
and through the connection of these two half-forms
(head and foot)
within each particular soul,
through this the connection of the head and foot of all of Israel is also accomplished, and their elevation before Hashem your G-d,
"You are standing today"
(Rosh Hashanah)
"all of you before Hashem your G-d: your heads... until your woodcutters and water drawers,"
that all of Israel
[the "head" of Israel
("your heads")
and the "foot" of Israel
("your woodcutters and water drawers")]
are connected together and they stand and are elevated before Hashem your G-d,
and they become one thing with Him, as the verse continues,
"to pass into the covenant...," for the matter of the covenant is that they become one thing.
